staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged checkout. The metadata vulnerable commit is `433d219ecae71f87585fb48bfd506e72127b15e5`, but the live prepared tree above is the exact source whose line map matches the saved ASan crash in `speech.c`, `setlengths.c`, and `synthdata.c`.

classification.classification_note: The sample metadata labels this benchmark `CWE-787`, but the saved sanitizer report is a `READ of size 8` before the start of `InterpretPhoneme2`'s stack `plist` object. This GT classifies the witnessed bug as an out-of-bounds read / stack-buffer-underflow.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42506685 (espeak-ng): Stack-buffer-underflow READ 8 found by fuzz target ssml-fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42506685
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / reproduction_report.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / staged vulnerable source under `_work/src/espeak-ng` / staged `poc` / patch.diff
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged 71-byte witness is copied by `ssml-fuzzer`, NUL-terminated, and passed to `espeak_Synth` with `espeakCHARS_UTF8 | espeakPHONEMES | espeakSSML`. `Synthesize()` admits that buffer through `text_decoder_decode_string_multibyte()`. The saved ASan stack returns to `Synthesize()` at `speech.c:457`, so the crash happens during the initial `SpeakNextClause(0)` for the first clause derived from that decoded input. `SpeakNextClause()` processes that clause by calling `TranslateClause()`, then `CalcPitches()`, then `CalcLengths()` (`synthesize.c:1569-1572`). `TranslateClause()` terminates the clause and `MakePhonemeList()` materializes the live `phoneme_list`, but `CalcPitches()` can still assign or rewrite `tone_ph` on that live list at `intonation.c:812-813`, `845`, `858`, `872`, `874`, `877`, `882`, `884`, `886`, and `918`. With `runtime_disambiguation` disabled, the staged artifacts do not isolate which pre-`CalcLengths()` write produced the crashing syllable's final nonzero selector, so the first directly witnessed selector is `CalcLengths()`'s `if (p->tone_ph != 0)` at `setlengths.c:711`. The same nonzero field is then passed to `InterpretPhoneme2(p->tone_ph, &phdata_tone)` at line 749. `InterpretPhoneme2()` creates a local `PHONEME_LIST plist[4]`, zeroes every `sourceix`, fills `plist[1]` with the requested phoneme, and sets only `plist[2].sourceix = 1` before calling `InterpretPhoneme(NULL, 0, &plist[1], ...)`. The selected phoneme program then evaluates a vowel-position condition through `InterpretCondition()`; the saved crash stack proves this reaches `CountVowelPosition()`, and in this source file only `isFirstVowel` and `isSecondVowel` call that helper. `CountVowelPosition()` counts vowels while walking backward until `sourceix != 0`, but on this temporary list both `plist[1].sourceix` and `plist[0].sourceix` are zero and there is no backward lower-bound check before `plist--`. The loop therefore decrements from `&plist[1]` to `&plist[0]` and then to `&plist[-1]`, and the next `plist->ph->type` read at `synthdata.c:473` triggers the saved AddressSanitizer stack-buffer-underflow. The staged `patch.diff` only changes phoneme-table data in `phsource/ph_russian`, `phsource/ph_serbian`, and `phsource/phonemes` plus tests; it does not touch the crashing control, tone-selection, or bounds logic in `synthesize.c`, `intonation.c`, `setlengths.c`, or `synthdata.c`, so Stage 02 cannot treat it as direct remediation evidence for this reproduced underflow.

source.description: Source. `Synthesize()` is the first project statement that consumes the harness-provided byte buffer by handing it to the text decoder under the SSML and phoneme-input flag configuration used by `ssml-fuzzer`.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact 71-byte file at `gt_results/arvo_42506685/poc` with SHA-256 `5ba4d7521cda524d56ef654ed545dd9559b7535a85aea3b189b5e4356b0adefc`. The witness contains no embedded NUL bytes, so after the harness appends one terminator and passes `size + 1` to `espeak_Synth`, this statement admits all 71 attacker bytes plus the appended terminator into the project decoder.
source.note: In the saved run the same `flags` also enabled `espeakSSML` and `espeakPHONEMES`, so downstream clause and phoneme logic interpret the admitted bytes under SSML- and phoneme-enabled parsing rules.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `CountVowelPosition()` relies only on seeing a backward `sourceix != 0` marker and never checks that `plist` is still inside the temporary four-entry array before decrementing. `InterpretPhoneme2()` provides only a forward marker at `plist[2]`, so the backward walk can step from `plist[0]` to `plist[-1]`.
root_cause.note: This invariant mismatch is already hinted at elsewhere in the project: `phonemelist.c:315-316` comments that reusing temporary list entries is safe only because normal code does not look backwards from that list shape, but `CountVowelPosition()` does.

sink.description: ASan crash site. After the unchecked backward walk has underflowed to `plist[-1]`, `CountVowelPosition()` dereferences the out-of-bounds `plist->ph` pointer and reads its `type` field.
sink.note: The saved ASan report shows `READ of size 8` at `synthdata.c:473`, with the bad address at offset 0 before `InterpretPhoneme2`'s local stack object `plist` (`[32, 192)` at line 986).

tainted_value_origin.description: This is the first directly witnessed vulnerability-relevant selector on the crashing syllable: `CalcLengths()` observes `p->tone_ph != 0` before using that selector for tone-specific length logic and later passing the same field to `InterpretPhoneme2()`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: During the initial `SpeakNextClause(0)` path, `TranslateClause()` materializes the live `phoneme_list` and `CalcPitches()` runs before `CalcLengths()`. Because `CalcPitches()` can assign or rewrite `tone_ph` at `intonation.c:812-813`, `845`, `858`, `872`, `874`, `877`, `882`, `884`, `886`, and `918`, and `run_flags.json` disables runtime disambiguation, Stage 02 cannot isolate the last writer that made this syllable's selector nonzero and anchors the selector here instead.

parser_admitted.description: The saved vulnerable run reaches the project text-decoder path under `espeakCHARS_UTF8 | espeakPHONEMES | espeakSSML` before clause and phoneme state are derived from the admitted witness.

first_clause.description: The saved ASan stack returns through the initial clause-processing call, so the reproduced sink is reached while processing the first clause emitted from the admitted witness. Inside `SpeakNextClause()`, the source runs `TranslateClause()`, then `CalcPitches()`, then `CalcLengths()` (`synthesize.c:1569-1572`).

evidence_limitations: The staged reproducer checkout is git `be962b067b889852da6194342b26e1759e1d7952`, which differs from the metadata vulnerable commit `433d219ecae71f87585fb48bfd506e72127b15e5`. This GT is grounded in the exact staged tree whose lines match the saved ASan trace.

`run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to `false`. Stage 02 can prove that `SpeakNextClause()` runs `CalcPitches()` before `CalcLengths()` and that `CalcPitches()` contains live `tone_ph` writes at `intonation.c:812-813`, `845`, `858`, `872`, `874`, `877`, `882`, `884`, `886`, and `918`, but it cannot statically determine whether the nonzero selector first observed at `setlengths.c:711` came from earlier `TranslateWord2()`/`MakePhonemeList()` state or from one of those `CalcPitches()` writes.

The staged `patch.diff` changes only phoneme-table data and tests. It may at most avoid one trigger-specific table configuration, but it does not modify the vulnerable path's control, tone-selection, or bounds logic in `phonemelist.c`, `synthesize.c`, `intonation.c`, `setlengths.c`, or `synthdata.c`, so `sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves` remains `false`.

coarse_trace.summary: `ssml-fuzzer` copies the exact witness, appends NUL, and calls `espeak_Synth` with UTF-8, phoneme-input, and SSML flags; `Synthesize()` admits those attacker bytes into the project text decoder.

The initial `SpeakNextClause(0)` call reaches `TranslateClause()`, which terminates the first clause and calls `MakePhonemeList()` to materialize the live `phoneme_list`. `SpeakNextClause()` then runs `CalcPitches()` before `CalcLengths()`, and `CalcPitches()` can assign or rewrite live `tone_ph` values at multiple `intonation.c` sites, so the last writer for the crashing syllable's selector is unresolved.

`CalcLengths()` is the first place where the crashing syllable's selector is directly observed: `p->tone_ph` is nonzero at `setlengths.c:711`, and the same field is passed to `InterpretPhoneme2()` at line 749.
`InterpretPhoneme2()` builds a four-entry local `plist`, leaves every backward `sourceix` zero, sets only `plist[2].sourceix = 1`, and then interprets the selected phoneme program at `&plist[1]`.
A vowel-position condition in that isolated phoneme program calls `CountVowelPosition()`, whose backward scan underflows past `plist[0]` and crashes on the next `plist->ph->type` read.

fine_trace.note: Source step. The exact 71-byte witness is admitted into the project text decoder here. In the saved run the same `flags` also enabled `espeakSSML` and `espeakPHONEMES`, so later synthesis stages parse the admitted bytes under those enabled input modes.

During the first-clause path, `SpeakNextClause()` runs `CalcPitches()` after `TranslateClause()`/`MakePhonemeList()` and before `CalcLengths()`. This stage can assign or rewrite live `tone_ph` fields at `intonation.c:812-813`, `845`, `858`, `872`, `874`, `877`, `882`, `884`, `886`, and `918`, so Stage 02 cannot statically identify which pre-`CalcLengths()` write produced the crashing syllable's final selector.

This is the first directly witnessed nonzero selector on the crashing syllable. By the time `CalcLengths()` reaches this entry, `p->tone_ph` is nonzero, so the tone-specific path executes and immediately dereferences `phoneme_tab[p->tone_ph]->std_length` at lines 712-714. Because `CalcPitches()` may have mutated the field earlier, Stage 02 anchors the selector here rather than at `phonemelist.c:514`.

Without any intervening `p->tone_ph` mutation inside `CalcLengths()`, the same nonzero selector is passed into `InterpretPhoneme2()`, which interprets that tone phoneme in isolation for this syllable.

A fixed-size four-entry stack array is created and zero-filled. That leaves every `sourceix` field at 0, while all four slots initially point at the pause phoneme; the array extent is exactly `plist[0]` through `plist[3]`.

The requested phoneme is installed at `plist[1]`, and the only word-boundary marker added to this temporary list is the forward marker `plist[2].sourceix = 1`. Both `plist[1].sourceix` and `plist[0].sourceix` remain zero, so there is still no backward sentinel before the starting pointer.
The generic phoneme-program interpreter is called on `&plist[1]`, i.e. the middle of this temporary four-entry list rather than a full phoneme list with an earlier start-of-word marker.

The selected phoneme program evaluates a vowel-position predicate on the isolated list. The staged artifacts do not disambiguate whether the exact opcode was `isFirstVowel` or `isSecondVowel`, but these are the only `InterpretCondition()` cases that call `CountVowelPosition(plist)`, matching the saved crash stack `InterpretCondition -> CountVowelPosition`.

Root-cause step. `CountVowelPosition()` stops only on `sourceix != 0`; it has no lower-bound check before `plist--`. Starting from `&plist[1]`, the first iteration sees `plist[1].sourceix == 0` and decrements to `&plist[0]`; the second sees `plist[0].sourceix == 0` and decrements again to `&plist[-1]`.

Sink. On the next loop iteration after step 9, `plist` already equals `&plist[-1]`, so reading `plist->ph->type` dereferences memory before the stack array and triggers the saved `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-underflow READ of size 8`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` changes only `phsource/ph_russian`, `phsource/ph_serbian`, `phsource/phonemes`, and `tests/language-phonemes.test`; it does not touch `phonemelist.c`, `synthesize.c`, `intonation.c`, `setlengths.c`, or `synthdata.c`, so Stage 02 has no patch-grounded remediation evidence for this reproduced crash path.

cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes, from the first directly witnessed selector in `CalcLengths()`. The staged source shows `p->tone_ph` is nonzero at `setlengths.c:711`, the same field is passed to `InterpretPhoneme2()` at line 749, and the saved ASan stack then continues through `InterpretCondition -> CountVowelPosition` to the sink. The exact earlier writer that made `p->tone_ph` nonzero remains unresolved because `CalcPitches()` can rewrite live `tone_ph` before `CalcLengths()`.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42506685 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed the staged `poc` to `/out/ssml-fuzzer` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-underflow READ of size 8` in `CountVowelPosition`.

format.name: Exact staged ssml-fuzzer witness
format.contract: The verified trigger is only the exact 71-byte file staged at `gt_results/arvo_42506685/poc` with SHA-256 `5ba4d7521cda524d56ef654ed545dd9559b7535a85aea3b189b5e4356b0adefc`, hex `ec819fed819f78819fed819f81afed819fed819f78819fed819f81afe19a80b0812cf3e0b49dcffde0b49de0b49dcf0de0f381a001745681a001015601e280ed819fed80819fed`. `ssml-fuzzer` copies those bytes, appends one NUL byte, and calls `espeak_Synth` with `espeakCHARS_UTF8 | espeakPHONEMES | espeakSSML`. In the saved vulnerable run that exact witness reaches the initial `SpeakNextClause(0)` clause, `SpeakNextClause()` runs `CalcPitches()` before `CalcLengths()`, and `CalcLengths()` then first observes a nonzero `p->tone_ph` on the crashing syllable at `setlengths.c:711` before passing the same field to `InterpretPhoneme2()` at line 749. The staged artifacts do not identify whether that nonzero selector came from earlier `TranslateWord2()`/`MakePhonemeList()` state or from one of the live `CalcPitches()` rewrites in `intonation.c`, and they do not justify a broader class of SSML strings, phoneme-input strings, or phoneme-table switches.
